ops.title: User declines defensive hardening layers around dependency-level fixes — fix the root cause minimally, no guard code or meta-tests unless asked
ops.body:
For the macFUSE-shadows-fuse-t bug (2026-06-11), offered full hardening (post-mount fstype assertion, missing-dylib fail-fast, `ccp doctor` fuse-t/macFUSE diagnostics, a go.mod version-pin regression test) vs just the cgofuse version bump. User chose: "just bump the version for this and any other deps that could benefit from it" and explicitly "no need for a test for this."

**Why:** consistent with the standing no-back-compat/no-migration-code rule in [[claude-pool-project]] — the user wants the root cause fixed at its source, not layers of defensive code guarding against its recurrence.

**How to apply:** when a bug traces to a dependency or config, propose the minimal root-cause fix as the primary plan; offer guard layers/diagnostics/meta-tests as opt-in extras, and expect them to be declined. Don't bundle them in by default.

**Refinement (2026-06-24, fusekit-holder Phase 1):** the no-guard rule holds even for guards that made it INTO an approved plan via adversarial verification. The plan (approved) included a structural `isTestBinary`/`ErrRefusedTestBinary` refusal guard in `proc.childCmd` (refuse to exec a `*.test` binary) as a fork-bomb backstop. User reaction: "get rid of all that test refusal, etc we agreed not to do any of that. your job here is to move it to the single holder/binary, not any of that other crap." The root-cause fix was the dedicated single holder binary (`cmd/holder` + `Spawn.ExecPath`) — which is never a test binary, so the guard was redundant defensive code. ALSO: "tone/trim down all the crazy long comments all over fusekit" — keep godoc/comments terse (1–3 lines), not multi-paragraph essays. Lesson: when authoring a plan, do NOT let adversarial-verification mitigations add guard layers / meta-tests / verbose rationale comments; the user strips them. Default to the minimal root-cause mechanism + terse comments, even when a workflow's skeptic pass argues for belt-and-suspenders.

**Refinement (2026-06-15, daemon CPU/401 plan):** "minimal" means *root cause at the source*, NOT fewest-lines. Given a choice for the heal-loop idle-load fix, the user picked the daemon-driven approach (the holder probes blindly because it lacks session info → give it that info; more plumbing — a new RPC + probe-on-assign) OVER a one-line interval bump or an in-holder health-backoff counter, calling the backoff "shim-like." For the split-daemon-ownership thrash they picked recover-now + verify-existing-prevention over adding new auto-recovery eviction code (which would touch a load-bearing safety invariant). So: prefer the change that removes the actual cause even if it's larger; reject backoff/retry/counter shims and defensive eviction layers even when they're shorter.
